key_insight: RareDx improves rare-disease ranking by combining controlled evidence use with knowledge-graph-grounded policy optimization, helping a compact model avoid plausible but invalid diagnoses.
clinical_relevance: This could support clinicians by surfacing better-ranked rare-disease candidates from fragmented phenotype, gene, and ontology evidence, but it is a decision-support tool rather than a standalone diagnostic.
method: Normalizes heterogeneous records into a shared ranked-diagnosis benchmark.
Uses knowledge-graph-grounded policy optimization with rewards based on curated relevance, ontology proximity, biomedical similarity, and phenotype consistency.
Adds vocabulary and output-length constraints to reduce fabricated or overlong differential diagnoses.
evidence_signal: Across eight benchmarks, the Qwen3.5-9B system reached 38.34 macro Hit@10, with a 1.60-point gain over GPT-5.5 under the archived protocol, and the 27B system achieved 23.53/36.56/40.76 Hit@1/5/10.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the underlying knowledge graph and benchmark routing, so real-world deployment may be less reliable when evidence is incomplete or atypical.
paper_title: RareDx: Controlled Knowledge Integration and Graph-Grounded Policy Optimization for Rare-Disease Diagnosis
